title: v1/chat.completions: stream coordinator and stop-token precedence for OpenAI parity
author: Evelyn Torres
description:
Summary: Align OpenAI /v1/chat.completions streaming behavior with non-streaming parity for stop tokens, logprobs attribution, and function/tool-call framing. This PR introduces a stream coordinator that enforces explicit frame boundaries around tool/function calls, adds a deterministic stop-token precedence rule (stop tokens are applied before emitting a function-call frame), and remaps per-token logprobs to the final emitted token stream so streaming and non-streaming responses match. Motivation: several customers reported mismatches in outputs/metrics between streaming and non-streaming paths (duplicate tokens, off-by-one logprob attribution), and streaming clients experienced idle timeouts on long generations. The coordinator also emits periodic heartbeat frames to keep long-lived streams alive.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement stream coordinator with heartbeats and backpressure signals.
- [x] Add stop-token precedence: runtime applies stop candidates before function-call envelope emission.
- [x] Rework logprob mapping so partial buffer tokens are consolidated to emitted tokens.
- [x] Add OpenAI-compat adapter changes in SDKs (Python adapter shim) and update docs.
- [x] Integration tests + fuzz cases for boundary conditions (stop inside tool call, consecutive stops, logprob rounding).
- [x] Add canary + perf benchmarks to validate ~<2% latency impact at typical batch sizes.

Design notes: The coordinator lives between the model output layer and the stream encoder. It watches the model token stream, applies stop rules with clear precedence (explicit stop tokens > role-based termination > EOS), and when a function call is detected will buffer until the call envelope is complete unless a higher-precedence stop token arrived. To avoid client timeouts the coordinator sends a small "heartbeat" SSE entry every 8s when no new emission would otherwise be sent. Logprobs: earlier streaming path emitted logprobs for intermediate tokens; new behavior aggregates logprob contributions so that the token logprob attached to an emitted token equals the final model-state logprob that would be produced on the non-streaming path.

Backward compatibility: The HTTP contract for /v1/chat.completions is unchanged; streaming framing is additive (clients that parse raw text continue to behave the same except they will not see duplicated trailing tokens when stop tokens overlap function boundaries). A new query param "stream_compat=stable" can be passed to opt-in to the strict OpenAI parity mode; for now we enable it by default for hosted customers to reduce customer-facing divergence.

Risks & mitigations: There is a small CPU overhead for heartbeat and additional buffering; we added workload-aware batching to keep P99 latency regressions < 2% and ran a 24h canary. We validated against a suite of 1800 prompt permutations.

release_notes: Stream coordinator: improved streaming parity with /v1/chat.completions. Stop tokens now have deterministic precedence and are applied consistently across streaming and non-streaming paths. Function-call frames are bounded and do not emit when a higher-precedence stop token applies. Streaming emits periodic heartbeat frames to prevent client timeouts. Logprobs are remapped to final emitted tokens to match non-streaming outputs. Added opt-in raw_logprobs envelope for debugging. SDK adapters updated.
